newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Alcoa Australia says profit outlook firm.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa Australia says profit outlook firm.

text.p: Aluminium company Alcoa of Australia said on Thursday the outlook for the company's earnings for the next year was firm and the company was continuing to look at ways to reduce costs.
Asked about the earnings outlook for the company in the next 12 months after a book launch, Alcoa of Australia's chairman and managing director Roger Vines said: "I would say the outlook is firm."
Vines said the company was very sensitive to its cost structure and was looking for ways to reduce costs in every aspect of its operations.
Alcoa of Australia is 60 percent owned by Aluminum Co of America and 39.25 percent by WMC Ltd with QBE Insurance Group Ltd holding the balance.
The company reported a net profit of A$395 million in calendar 1996 and paid dividends of A$380 million.
Vines said the company's workforce would be reduced later next calendar year when it closed down its Jarrahdale mine in Western Australia.
A spokesman from the company's Perth headquarters told Reuters the decision to close the mine 18 months from now was made in February.
"Jarrahdale is the oldest of the three (bauxite) mines that supply the Kwinana (aluminium) refinery. It has old technology and it our highest cost producer," the spokesman said.
The spokesman said the company had decided to spend A$88 million upgrading the Huntly mine which would be expanded to supply the Kwinana refinery as well as the Pinjarra refinery.
"When we say the closure of a mine it is not a reduction in production it is just being sourced elsewhere," he said.
The spokesman said about 200 people were currently being employed at the Jarrahdale mine and the Huntly expansion would require at least an additional 100 employees.
